question.text: For a Category III AIF dealing in listed equities and exchange-traded derivatives, Mark-to-Market valuation is crucial PRIMARILY because:

answer.text: It permits the manager to smooth NAV volatility by averaging prices across the week
It converts cash profits into notional profits for tax deferral
SEBI mandates MTM only for commodity futures, not equity futures
It ensures the NAV reflects current fair market value, enables fair Incentive Fee computation, and provides a fair redemption price to exiting unitholders

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 14.10.2, MTM ensures NAV reflects 'true worth' of portfolio on each valuation day. It is crucial for (i) fair Incentive Fee computation based on actual market returns; (ii) fair redemption/withdrawal prices for unitholders; (iii) daily reconciliation of derivative margin accounts with brokers. The Trap: Option A is factually wrong. Option C ('smoothing') is the OPPOSITE of MTM and would be manipulation. Option D is nonsensical — MTM has no tax-deferral effect. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Derivatives) covers MTM mechanics; XIX-C centres on the investor-protection angle (fair incentive fee, fair redemption). Manager's Pro-Tip: Audit your MTM snapshot time. A fund manager marking at 3:30 pm for F&O positions vs 3:25 pm for cash equity vs NAV published at T+1 creates tiny arbitrages. Lock down a single intraday timestamp in the Valuation Policy.
